frozen.title: Identification counts as complete only when every animal is entered, and submit needs one entry per species when several are selected
frozen.detail: Today the hub's Identification details row shows Complete straight after Commodity details, before any animal is identified, and stays Complete at 1 of 2. DR2.1 counts identification complete only when every animal of every selected species with identifier fields has a complete entry. For submitting, DR2.1 makes identification optional for a single species but needs at least one complete entry per species when more than one species is selected; the identification page itself shows no message for that rule.
acceptanceCriteria: Straight after Commodity details, with no animals entered, the hub's Identification details row does not show Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-002; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p10-003-m1)

With 1 of 2 cattle entered, the row does not show Complete; once both are entered with ear tag and passport it shows Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-066)
A selected species with identifier fields but no number of animals keeps the row from showing Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068)
With one species selected and no identification entered, the notification can be submitted. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070)

With two species with identifier fields selected and one of them without any complete entry, submitting is refused; once each has at least one complete entry, submitting goes ahead. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-020)
The identification page shows no message about the submit rule. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070)
notes: Combines the hub completion rule and the submit rule: both read the same 'complete entry' definition from the every-identifier row and change the same obligation evaluation. The submit refusal's place and wording belong to the review-and-submit area, which owns the submit gate and its messages (req-animal-identification-056's why); the criterion asserts only that submitting is refused or goes ahead. If that area drafts a row for the same gate, the combiner should merge this submit criterion into it or set dependsOn. The germinal half of the completion rule (a germinal species counts once its entry is saved) is proved in the germinal panel row. Builds after the every-identifier row in this area.

Dropped: req-248 and req-249 are adopted as already met. ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claims 13, 36 and 37 split off their germinal halves and settle that one identifier is enough for Complete and for submit, which the live-animals code does today; the germinal bar is req-261 in inc-183.
